rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here sūra means a piece or portion in its lexical sense: the hypothetical challenge has no external counterpart bearing the technical name.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالسورة هنا مفهومها اللغوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The technical sense of sūra was known only to believers; had the challenge meant a Qur'anic sūra as a technical unit, it would have said to bring its like from the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: ولأن معرفة المعنى الاصطلاحي كانت مخصوصا بالمصدقين ولو أريد التحدي بسورة من القرآن لقيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this lexical reading, the challenge confines them to calling witnesses who are present with them.
rows.anchor: ولما كان هذا هو المراد قصرهم في الدعاء على من بحضرتهم من الشهداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional phrase hints that their profession of doubt about the revelation is itself a lie.
rows.anchor: إيماء إلى كذبهم في دعوى الشك فيه

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī defines truthfulness as the tongue's statement and limbs' action matching what the heart contains as established reality.
rows.anchor: الصادق الذي يكون قول لسانه وعمل جوارحه

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī links the revelation's descent to the preceding provision: both are sustenance, one outward and general, the other inward and specially bestowed on the most complete recipients.
rows.anchor: وقال : اتسقت آية تنزيل الوحي بآية إنزال الرزق

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Outward provision descends generally, even to unbelievers, whereas revelation is inward provision reserved for the elect; a challenge tests the claim of exclusive bestowal.
rows.anchor: لأنهما رزقان : أحدهما ظاهر يعم الكافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they dispute the Prophet's special selection, they may suppose revelation is general and attempt to match it; their failure demonstrates the selection.
rows.anchor: فإن نازعهم ريب في الاختصاص فيفرضون أنه عام فيحاولون معارضته

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Calling the Prophet God's servant displays his thorough humility and distinctive submission, the reason for his special election.
rows.anchor: وأجرى ذكره باسم العبودية إعلاما بوفائه بأنحاء التذلل وإظهارا لمزية انفراده بذلك دونهم

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The plural in 'We sent down' encompasses the attendants who bring revelation, such as the Holy Spirit and the Trustworthy Spirit, and implies their following.
rows.anchor: وانتظم النون في { نزلنا } من يتنزل بالوحي

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The plural in 'Our servant' points to the Prophet's obedience, following, humility, and willingness to accept a correct view from his community.
rows.anchor: واقتضت النون في لفظ { عبدنا } ما يظهره النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لهم من الانقياد والاتباع

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet's humility even in eating is illustrated by his saying that he eats as a servant eats.
rows.anchor: في أكله كما قال : ( آكل كما يأكل العبد )

rows.speaker: جلال الدين محمد بن أحمد المحلي
rows.claim: Al-Maḥallī says the challenge includes the shortest sūra, such as al-Kawthar, or an independent verse equal to it, or multiple verses.
rows.anchor: كما قاله الإمام جلال الدين محمد بن أحمد المحلي في شرح جمع الجوامع

rows.speaker: شمس الدين محمد بن عبد الدائم البرماوي
rows.claim: Al-Barmawī had already formulated the view that the challenge can be met by a verse-sized portion; he transmits support from the apparent wording of al-Juwaynī and jurists' dowry rulings.
rows.anchor: وسبقه الإمام شمس الدين محمد بن عبد الدائم البرماوي فنظمه في القنية في الأصول

rows.speaker: سعد الدين مسعود بن عمر التفتازاني
rows.claim: Al-Taftāzānī states that the miraculous unit is a sūra or an equivalent amount, reflecting the usual account that the challenge was to produce a sūra.
rows.anchor: في تلويحه على توضيح صدر الشريعة : المعجز هو السورة أو مقدارها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Biqāʿī corrects that account: the challenge was to produce a portion of a verse or more, because sūra here has its lexical rather than technical meaning.
rows.anchor: والصواب أنه إنما وقع بقطعة آية فما فوقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrites had found Qur'anic parables strange and treated as doubtful what should have convinced them, arguing that God would not use such examples.
rows.anchor: وكانوا قد استغربوا بعض أمثال القرآن وجعلوها موضعا للشك من حيث كانت موضعا لليقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge answers determined opponents rather than sincere doubters: it declares their inability lasting and makes their hostility plain.
rows.anchor: وأخبرهم بأنهم عاجزون عنها وأن عجزهم دائم تحقيقا لأنهم في ذلك الحال معاندون لا شاكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional 'if you do not' grants them a respite in wording and mocks their presumed ability, exposing their ignorance.
rows.anchor: فأتى بأداة الشك تنفيسا لهم وتهكما في نفس الأمر بهم واستجهالا لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic prediction then strikes decisively: God rules that they will fail, and their silence confirms the verdict across every age.
rows.anchor: ثم لم يتمم ذلك التنفيس حتى ضربهم ضربة فضمت ظهورهم وقطعت قلوبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They had no effective response except to stop attempting the challenge, thereby verifying the prophecy of failure.
rows.anchor: فلم يكن لهم فعل إلا المبادرة إلى تصديقه بالكف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word 'do' is broader than 'bring': denying the general act also denies the more specific act of producing a rival.
rows.anchor: والتعبير بالفعل الأعم من الإتيان أبلغ لأن نفيه نفي الأخص وزيادة

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī defines action as what appears from a prompting circumstance, whether done knowingly or not, religiously or otherwise.
rows.anchor: والفعل قال الحرالي ما ظهر عن داعية من الموقع كان عن علم أو غير علم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book that guides to the straight path is the greatest proof of God's exclusive divinity and the exclusive worship and watchfulness owed to Him.
rows.anchor: فقد ثبت أن هذا الكتاب الذي بين أنه الهادي إلى الصراط المستقيم أعظم دليل على إفراده بالعبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an's inimitability proves God's exclusive divinity and worship, joined to the prayer of al-Fātiḥa 1:4 for worship and help from God alone.
rows.anchor: إياك نعبد وإياك نستعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Neither the Arabs nor fluent Jews and Christians who lived among them could answer the challenge, despite their eloquence, learning, and accomplished poets.
rows.anchor: بما ثبت من عجزهم عن معارضته وعجز جميع العرب الذين كانوا أفصح الخلق وكذا جميع من ولد في بلادهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The only would-be rivals named are Musaylima and al-Aswad al-ʿAnsī; their attempts exposed them as liars and their disgrace became proverbial.
rows.anchor: إلا ما قاله مسيلمة والأسود العنسي فيما افتضحوا به وأكذبهم الله تعالى فيه

rows.speaker: عمرو بن بحر الجاحظ
rows.claim: Al-Jāḥiẓ says Muḥammad was sent when Arabs were at their height in poetry, oratory, linguistic mastery, and military strength, and called them to monotheism by proof.
rows.anchor: قال عمرو بن بحر الجاحظ ( في كتاب الحجة في تثبيت خبر الواحد ) إن الله تبارك وتعالى بعث محمدا

rows.speaker: عمرو بن بحر الجاحظ
rows.claim: Al-Jāḥiẓ says that after proof removed excuses, pride and desire rather than ignorance kept the opponents from accepting the message, so the conflict escalated to war.
rows.anchor: فلما قطع العذر وأزال الشبهة وصار الذي يمنعهم من الإقرار الهوى والحمية دون الجهل والحيرة حملهم على حظهم بالسيف

rows.speaker: عمرو بن بحر الجاحظ
rows.claim: Even amid deaths among leaders, relatives, companions, and family, the Prophet kept arguing from the Qur'an and inviting them to meet its challenge.
rows.anchor: وقتلوا أعمامه وبني أعمامه وعلية أصحابه وأعلام أهله

rows.speaker: عمرو بن بحر الجاحظ
rows.claim: Al-Jāḥiẓ reports that opponents alleged the Prophet knew histories unknown to them; he answered by inviting them to fabricate a rival, but no orator tried and no poet dared.
rows.anchor: أنت تعرف من أخبار الأمم ما لا نعرف فلذلك يمكنك ما لا يمكننا

rows.speaker: عمرو بن بحر الجاحظ
rows.claim: Al-Jāḥiẓ argues that a short rival sūra would have discredited the Prophet faster and at less cost than risking lives, exile, and wealth in war.
rows.anchor: لأن سورة واحدة وآيات يسيرة كانت أنقض لقوله وأفسد لأمره وأبلغ في تكذيبه

rows.speaker: عمرو بن بحر الجاحظ
rows.claim: Al-Jāḥiẓ says the Arabs' sustained failure over twenty-three years cannot be explained as a mistake or as knowingly abandoning an available response.
rows.anchor: أن يجتمع هؤلاء كلهم على الغلط في الأمر الظاهر والخطأ المكشوف البين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their failure silenced their eloquence and humbled their pride; a dependent, deficient creature cannot rival the One whose attributes are perfect.
rows.anchor: فثبت بهذا عجزهم وخرس قطعا إفصاحهم ورمزهم وطأطأ ذلا كبرهم وعزهم

rows.speaker: أبو سليمان الخطابي
rows.claim: Al-Khaṭṭābī's account, which al-Biqāʿī calls the best he found and says most speculative scholars adopted, locates inimitability in eloquence, though scholars struggled to specify it and often invoked taste.
rows.anchor: وأحسن ما وقفت عليه من ذلك ما نقله الإمام بدر الدين الزركشي الشافعي في كتابه البرهان عن الإمام أبي سليمان الخاطبي

rows.speaker: أبو سليمان الخطابي
rows.claim: Al-Khaṭṭābī distinguishes weighty elevated speech, simple eloquence, and fluent acceptable speech; the Qur'an draws from all three and uniquely unites grandeur with sweetness.
rows.anchor: فمنها البليغ الرصين الجزل

rows.speaker: أبو سليمان الخطابي
rows.claim: Al-Khaṭṭābī explains that humans cannot reproduce the Qur'an because they cannot master the full vocabulary, meanings, and patterns of arrangement needed to choose the best possible expression.
rows.anchor: وإنما تعذر على البشر جميعا الإتيان بمثله

rows.speaker: أبو سليمان الخطابي
rows.claim: Al-Khaṭṭābī says speech consists of a word carrying meaning and an ordering bond; the Qur'an excels in the vocabulary, composition, and meanings alike.
rows.anchor: وإنما يقوم الكلام بهذه الأشياء الثلاثة لفظ حامل ومعنى به قائم ورباط لهما ناظم

rows.speaker: أبو سليمان الخطابي
rows.claim: The Qur'an combines soundest meanings—monotheism, divine transcendence, worship, law, exhortation, ethics, history, and future events—in an arrangement that makes evidence and what it proves reinforce each other.
rows.anchor: مضمنا أصح المعاني من توحيد الله تعالى وتنزيه له في صفاته

rows.speaker: أبو سليمان الخطابي
rows.claim: Al-Khaṭṭābī concludes that bringing such disparate matters into coherent accord exceeds human power, so people cannot produce its like or a counterpart of its form.
rows.anchor: ومعلوم أن الإتيان بمثل هذه الأمور والجمع بين أشتاتها حتى تنتظم وتتسق أمر تعجز عنه قوى البشر

rows.speaker: أبو سليمان الخطابي
rows.claim: Opponents called it poetry because of its ordered sound and magic because they could not match it; its impact on hearts unsettled them, though they admitted its sweetness and beauty.
rows.anchor: ثم صار المعاندون له يقولون مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The charge that the Qur'an was copied from ancient tales conflicts with the opponents' knowledge that Muḥammad was unlettered and had no one present to dictate or write for him.
rows.anchor: مع علمهم أن صاحبه أمي وليس بحضرته من يملي أو يكتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Biqāʿī reads al-Khaṭṭābī's opening as emphasizing composition alone but his conclusion as combining composition and meaning; he endorses the latter for a one-sūra challenge.
rows.anchor: وأول كلامه يميل إلى أن الإعجاز بمجرد النظم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the challenge to ten sūras, the account transmitted by al-Baghawī from al-Mubarrad, like al-Jāḥiẓ's view, makes eloquence of composition the criterion.
rows.anchor: وأما بالعشر فبالنظر إلى البلاغة في النظم فقط

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says human expression falls short because human knowledge of present events is incomplete, knowledge of the past is further reduced by forgetting, and speech about the future is conjectural; God's account fully encompasses all three.
rows.anchor: وقال الأستاذ أبو الحسن الحرالي في مفتاح الباب المقفل الباب الأول

rows.speaker: محمد بن عبد الرحمن المراكشي الأكمه
rows.claim: Al-Marrākushī says the miraculous aspect is recognized by reflecting on the science of eloquence, which prevents errors or obscurity in conveying meaning and improves speech in keeping with context.
rows.anchor: وقال الإمام محمد بن عبد الرحمن المراكشي الأكمه في شرح نظمه لمصباح ابن مالك في المعاني والبيان

rows.speaker: محمد بن عبد الرحمن المراكشي الأكمه
rows.claim: Al-Marrākushī says the global evidence is that Arabs failed to match the Qur'an despite its being in their own language.
rows.anchor: فعلى إعجازه دليل إجمالي وهو أن العرب عجزت عنه وهو بلسانها

rows.speaker: محمد بن عبد الرحمن المراكشي الأكمه
rows.claim: Al-Marrākushī also rejects diversion from producing a rival as the cause, since audiences were struck by eloquence and would-be imitators produced repulsive, malformed speech.
rows.anchor: ولا بالصرف عن معارضته , لأن تعجبهم كان من فصاحته

rows.speaker: محمد بن عبد الرحمن المراكشي الأكمه
rows.claim: He says the detailed proof starts with reflection on the properties of the Qur'an's composition and ends in knowledge that it came from the All-Knowing.
rows.anchor: ودليل تفصيلي مقدمته التفكر في خواص تركيبه

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī describes the Fire as a subtle substance whose extreme action reverses ordinary states through intense heat or cold.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي , وهي جوهر لطيف يفرط لشدة لطافته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another definition calls it a luminous, hot body whose nature is to burn.
rows.anchor: جسم لطيف مضيء حار من شأنه الإحراق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stones include the idols the opponents paired with themselves in worldly worship; their failure and continued denial make them obstinate, and their idols will burn them without benefit or intercession.
rows.anchor: التي هي أعم من أصنامهم التي قرنوا بها أنفسهم في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite 'Fire' and its relative description present the Qur'an's divinely established report as certain, as though even what the audience does not know is universally known.
rows.anchor: وتعريف النار وصلة الموصول لأن أخبار القرآن بعد ثبوت أنه من عند الله معلومة مقطوع بها

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī explains stone as what has become hard through the compact joining of its water and earth components.
rows.anchor: الحجارة ما تحجر أي اشتد تصام أجزائه من الماء والتراب

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī glosses 'fear' as stopping the separation of God from His Messenger: they acknowledge God's lordship while doubting His Messenger.
rows.anchor: واتقوا } أي توقفوا عن هذه التفرقة بين الله ورسوله

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī sees the punishment as a fitting, painful separation of what should be joined; if they missed restraint guided by knowledge, they should heed restraint driven by pain.
rows.anchor: فإنها نار غذاؤها واشتعالها بالكون كله أنهاه تركيبا وهم الناس الملائمون لمارجها بالنوس

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Its human and stone fuel spans the extremes of created beings and implies a scope and power beyond worldly fire, which is fueled by plants and affects extremes only indirectly.
rows.anchor: وليست كنار الدنيا التي غذاؤها من ضعيف الموالد وهو النبات ولا تفعل في الطرفين إلا بواسطة

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī cites the fire brought from the green tree in Yā Sīn 36:80 and the Arab saying that every tree contains fire, especially marakh and ʿafār.
rows.anchor: وتقول العرب : في كل شجر نار واستمجد المرخ والعفار

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The word 'fuel' points to what fire acts on most intensely, since it mediates the fire's action on everything else; consuming the fuel strengthens the fire against it.
rows.anchor: لأن النار أشد فعلها في وقودها لأن بتوسطه تفعل فيما سواه

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says the punished are conceived as both generated from and nourished by the Fire; it is hidden in them in worldly life and blazing in the afterlife, each person bearing its measure.
rows.anchor: ويفهم اعتبارها بنار الدنيا انقداحها من أعمال المجزيين بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Biqāʿī supports the fiery-element analogy with the description of wasteful people as satanic brothers and the devils' incitement of unbelievers.
rows.anchor: أي في أن الغالب عليهم العنصر الناري

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī takes the stones to imply resurrection and judgment for all that the heavens and earth contain, not only humans and jinn; all creation is divided between Garden and Fire as between good and vile.
rows.anchor: وفي ذكر الحجارة إفهام عموم البعث والجزاء

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says belief initially emphasizes resurrection and recompense of the two weighty kinds for ease; belief about the rest is an increase and completion of faith.
rows.anchor: وإنما اقتصر في مبدأ عقيدة الإيمان على الإيمان ببعث الثقلين وجزائهم تيسيرا واستفتاحا

rows.speaker: بعض العلماء
rows.claim: Some scholars restrict resurrection and recompense to humans and jinn, deny reward to other creatures, and strain to reinterpret the report that a hornless sheep will receive justice from a horned sheep.
rows.anchor: حتى أن منهم من ينكر جزاء ما سواهما

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet reports that the hornless sheep will receive redress from the horned sheep.
rows.anchor: يقتص للشاة الجماء من الشاة القرناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Fire has been prepared and made ready before it is used, and it is prepared for the disbelievers and anyone who shares their trait of concealing God's signs.
rows.anchor: هيئت وأكملت قبل زمن استعمالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive voice leaves the preparer unnamed; al-Biqāʿī says an unknown perpetrator makes the complainant's grievance more painful.
rows.anchor: وتقاد للمجهول لأن المشتكي إذا جهل فاعله كان أنكأ

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī compares this prepared punishment to a worldly king's sword kept ready for its intended victims.
rows.anchor: وهي عدة الملك الديان لهم بمنزلة سيف الملك من ملوك الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After warning of punishment, the passage turns to the believers' reward; it shifts the address mercifully to the Prophet, leaving an implied command to warn them unstated.
rows.anchor: ولما ذكر ما لهم ترهيبا اتبعه ما للمؤمنين ترغيبا فقال صارفا وجه الخطاب بالرحمة إلى نبي الرحمة

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī defines glad tidings as revealing hidden happiness through speech.
rows.anchor: والبشرى قال الحرالي إظهار غيب المسرة بالقول

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī explains the believers here as those who affirm the messengers.
rows.anchor: آمنوا } أي صدقوا الرسل

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī defines action as conduct built on knowledge or its presumed equivalent, and righteous deeds as words and acts protected from defects.
rows.anchor: من العمل وهو فعل بني على علم أو زعمه

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī reasons that glad tidings are for someone still at risk, while believers are secure and therefore deserve something beyond glad tidings, up to the incomparable rank of iḥsān.
rows.anchor: وإذا كانت البشرى لهؤلاء فالمؤمنون أحق بما فوق البشرى

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī links the plural gardens to the multiple ranks of deeds, with reward matching their variety and degree.
rows.anchor: لتعدد رتب أفعالهم التي يطابق الجزاء ترتبها وتعددها

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When a woman asked about her son, the Prophet said there are gardens and that her son attained the highest Firdaws.
rows.anchor: قال عليه الصلاة والسلام للتي سألت عن ابنها : ( إنها جنان وإن ابنك أصاب الفردوس الأعلى )

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The phrase 'for them' suggests that the Garden properly joins their selves and completes their condition, while its delights gather the pleasures of the senses and conceal further, lasting bliss.
rows.anchor: وفي التعبير بلهم إشعار بأن ذلك الذي لهم ينبغي لحاقه بذواتهم ليحصل به من كمال أمرهم وصلاح حالهم

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī defines flowing as rapid, continuous movement.
rows.anchor: من الجري وهو إسراع حركة الشيء ودوامها

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī glosses 'beneath them' as beneath the chambers, below the level.
rows.anchor: من تحت غرفها , والتحت ما دون المستوى

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī defines rivers as broad channels for water.
rows.anchor: جمع نهر , وهو المجرى الواسع للماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying that the gardens flow is metaphorical; the definite article may refer to the familiar kind, or mean that each tree and chamber has a spring beneath it, keeping the gardens perpetually green and fruitful.
rows.anchor: والتعريف لما عهده السامع من الجنس

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says the workers' reward discloses that their deeds were founded on sincerity, for water is its sign of generative increase.
rows.anchor: وإذا تعرف حال العامل من وصف جزائه علم أن أعمالهم كانت مبنية على الإخلاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'Whenever' signals that the event recurs throughout all times.
rows.anchor: وهي كلمة تفهم تكرر الأمر في عموم الأوقات

words: قَالُوا۟ هَٰذَا ٱلَّذِى رُزِقْنَا مِن قَبْلُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fruit resembles what they knew in worldly life, so they recognize its kind; the passive 'they were given' leaves the giver unstated because it is not at issue.
rows.anchor: لكونه على صورة ما في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fruit's outward color and kind resemble one another, leading recipients to expect a familiar taste; its superior taste makes every serving a renewed delight.
rows.anchor: والتشابه المراد هنا اشتراك في ظاهر الصورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive wording indicates that the fruit is brought to them without their having to seek or yearn for it.
rows.anchor: جيء لهم بهذا الجنس المرزوق لهم في الدارين في الجنة من غير تطلب وتشوق

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī takes 'before' to mean that individual fruits do not differ in rank and are rapidly replaced after picking, so each replacement looks like the one taken.
rows.anchor: جعل الحرالي هذا خاصا بثمار الجنة فقال : من قبل إعلام

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says of a cluster in Paradise that, had he taken it, people could have eaten from it for as long as the world lasted.
rows.anchor: قال عليه السلام في عنقود من ثمرها : ( لو أخذته لأكلتم منه ما بقيت الدنيا )

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī sees continuous replenishment as suggesting that believers' intentions in their deeds were constant and steadfast, producing complete, continuous reward.
rows.anchor: ويشعر ذلك عند اعتبار العمل به بأن نياتهم في الأعمال صالحة ثابتة مرابطة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A marfūʿ report transmitted by al-Ṭabarānī from Sahl ibn Saʿd says, 'A believer's intention is better than his deed.'
rows.anchor: ومنه حديث مرفوع أخرجه الطبراني عن سهل بن سعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The resemblance also removes anxiety: unlike worldly selection, recipients need not fear getting an inferior fruit or labor to choose the best.
rows.anchor: أظهر عذرهم في توهم اتحاد الثمر وعرف بأمنتهم من العنا

rows.speaker: بعض العلماء
rows.claim: Some scholars hold that every Paradise fruit resembles every other even when their varieties differ; al-Biqāʿī considers this weak because it would erase the next verse's full distinction in meaning and form.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكر بعض العلماء اطراد هذا التشابه في ثمر الجنة وإن اختلفت أصنافه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Biqāʿī weakens the view that all different fruit varieties resemble one another, since it would entail complete correspondence in both meaning and appearance.
rows.anchor: ويضعفه ما يلزم منه كمال الدلالة في المعنى والصورة
